text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - London stocks finished back below the 4,000 level as Wall Street and re-awakening fears of domestic interest rates rises left shares to struggle through a jittery session on Tuesday. traders said. Under pressure from the start after a sharp reversal in U.S. stocks overnight, stronger-than-expected UK money supply figures added to the downbeat mood and was reinforced by another disappointing performance in New York in the afternoon. The FTSE 100 closed at 3,993.5, a fall of 31.8 points but above the day's lows of 3,988.9.

FRANKFURT- German shares closed floor trade weaker on Tuesday after the dollar weakened against the mark and as Wall Street losses and comments by German economic institutes held the market back. The DAX index of 30 leading shares reversed gains made on Monday when it had reached above the crucial 2,700 point mark, to end down 30.21 points at 2,673.62. In post-bourse trade the index fell 27.83 to 2,675.50.

PARIS - French stocks fell 1.15 percent on Tuesday after weakness in the dollar, bond prices and concerns that German interest rates may rise drove the bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index through important support levels. The CAC-40 index finished down 24.65 points at 2,125.74.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended markedly lower, but off the day's lows in quiet trade as sagging futures on blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) put pressure on the stocks. Weaker-than-expected U.S. consumer confidence data lent shares some support in the second half of the session, but investors were likely to remain sidelined ahead of U.S. presidential elections, a dealer said. "We may see a further decline in prices", he added. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) lost 19.46 points to 2,395.80 points.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed firmer, lifted by buying of export-related shares that benefit from a weaker yen. The benchmark Nikkei 225 settled at 20,958.08, up 72.67 points.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Tuesday due to profit-taking in leading shares and some futures-related activity. The Hang Seng Index finished 70.60 points down at 12,192.17, but 20 points off its low for the day of 12,172.84.

SYDNEY - Australian shares drifted down to end near their lows on Tuesday as investors showed caution ahead of the release of key U.S. economic data later this week and after the Dow and base metals prices softened on Monday. The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed down 11.1 points at 2,323.0, just off its intra-day low of 2,320.6.

JOHANNESBURG - Heavy futures-related trade pushed South African shares to close, fuelled by concerns on a struggling rand which tested another all-time low on the dollar. Gold shares weakened on poor sentiment about the rand. Dealers said futures players were dominant, responsible for over 50 percent of the trade. They said foreigners were absent in the market since the currency devaluation eroded whatever profits they made on equities. The overall index fell 96.3 points to 6,868 points and the industrial index dropped 106.8 points to 8,114.4 points and gold index slipped 11.7 points to end at 1,706 points.
